newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU grain export commitments exceed 20 million T.
newsitem.headline: EU grain export commitments exceed 20 million T.

text.p: European Union grain export commitments up to February 18 are up 49 percent over last year, official figures showed on Friday.

Figures supplied by member country officials showed grain earmarked for export between July 1, 1996 and February 18, 1997 totalled 20.728 million tonnes against 13.897 million during the same period last year.
Exports of commercial soft wheat grain reached 7.074 million tonnes against 4.6 million a year ago.
Soft wheat flour exports jumped to 4.736 million tonnes from 3.468 million while barley exports reached 4.264 million tonnes against 1.244 million.
Last year exports were hurt by low stocks and a rare export tax to help control high domestic prices.
On Thursday the European Union awarded 238,000 tonnes of soft wheat, 138,500 tonnes of barley and 10,000 tonnes of maize for export to non-EU countries.

The EU grain trade lobby Coceral has forecast that based on a record crop of 203.1 million tonnes, the EU can export 25.8 million tonnes of grain and processed products in the 1996/97 season ending on June 30.
This would include 15 million tonnes in wheat and processed products.
